correctness.rationale: In odd characteristic the regular octad marking gives the six-dimensional even-subset quotient with intersection-parity pairing and equivariant two-subsets for bitangents. The matching class contains four weight-two vectors and recovers the underlying matching. The complementary family consists of affine hyperplane systems (the full set of hyperplanes recovers the affine structure), each a totally isotropic three-space with no weight-two vector. The 105 and 30 therefore exhaust the symplectic count 135. An independently written RREF enumeration and power-fixed-point inversion (python3 /workspace/branches/de3036dd-d737-4491-8f27-753cd05dcaff/independent_gopel_check.py; output independent_gopel_check.out in the same directory) reproduced all 22 frozen rows, the fixed-column split, and the bitangent counts. The uploaded code was not run. Frobenius stability of a kernel is finite étale descent, not pointwise rationality of its constituent torsion points. Orbit lengths count closed point degrees and yield the finite étale zeta product and extension counts. Neither the proof nor the check asserts realization of all partitions over any specified field.

originality.rationale: The exact action and the numerical information needed to recover every frozen row are already represented in the inspected sources. The distinct same-day record 965aa47ed270 gives all 22 cycle profiles on the 30 affine structures AND the fixed-point counts on the 105 matchings for all 22 classes of the same S_8 action. The hyperelliptic versus quartic distinction does not change the permutation actions: both are built functorially from the same eight-element set, and the stable-octad identification is known independently for quartics. Möbius inversion on powers of each partition recovers the entire 105-point cycle profile from that table.
